Dip hop—a growing subgenre of hip hop grounded
in Deaf culture and aesthetics—challenge stereotypes
and help to reshape mainstream notions of what music
is. Fundamental to the style are a heavy emphasis on
bass beats and lyrics rapped in sign language such as
ASL (American Sign Language). Audiences feel the
rhythmic vibrations, see the lyrics in motion, and
Though rooted in hip hop, dip hop is not simply
rap songs translated into ASL but musical expression
from a Deaf perspective; artists craft original songs
and develop individual styles. Some collaborate with
DJs, deaf or hearing, some induct visual elements
like sound-activated lights, and some use specialized
